chapter_title: The Catechumen asks the Apostle: will Rest come about for Someone who has come out of the Body, if the Saints pray over and make an Alms-offering for him?
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional material about prayer for the dead, alms-offerings, and remembrances — classic ecclesiastical practice. The oldest teaching layer survives in two well-preserved cosmological narrative blocks (¶8-14: Mother of Life's supplication and First Man's rescue; ¶17-22: Five Fathers' supplication and Third Ambassador's emanation) plus fragmented third and fourth archetypal episodes (¶25-27: Jesus the Splendour). These emanation narratives describe events entirely within the cosmic system and closely parallel cosmogony found elsewhere in the corpus. The editor repurposed these pre-existing narratives as archetypal precedents for institutional practice, inserting editorial bridge paragraphs ('just as the Mother of Life was granted... so too the saints') and extensive institutional application (four victories of prayer, analogy of the bound relative, catechumen commission). The editorial fatigue pattern is strong: substrate is front-loaded (first half 6.47), institutional accumulates in the second half (7.56). Teaching purity 0.392 reflects the heavy institutional overlay.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic opening: 'Once again, it happened one time while our enlightener is sitting in the midst of the congregation.' Standard Kephalaia session-opening formula with hagiographic attribution.

Catechumen's question about prayer for the dead. 'I beseech you, my master' is standard honorific formula. The question is about institutional practice (efficacy of prayer for the deceased), not cosmic structure. No substrate content to extract.

Continuation of the catechumen's question. Raises the doctrinal tension between intercession and retribution ('each one shall receive retribution according to his deeds'). While doctrinally substantive, this is framed as 'we have heard from you' — recitation of received teaching within the dialogue frame, not systematic cosmic exposition.
Pure frame formula: 'I beseech you my master, that you may instruct me.' 'It is very great and honoured amongst people' references contemporary social valuation — the editorial present.

Opens with dialogue frame ('Then the apostle speaks to him'). Content is institutional teaching about prayer efficacy: 'every elect person, if he beseeches charity in total faith' — describes community practice. 'Our compassionate Father' as addressee of petition. No cosmic-correspondential mapping; this teaches what the elect should do, not what cosmic beings ARE.

Classic editorial bridge: connects cosmic archetype ('the gods first made entreaty of their Father') to institutional present ('the holy church that assumes the flesh is established in prayer and entreaty above all'). One side cosmos, other side contemporary institution. The brief cosmic allusion is not systematic teaching but an editorial summary serving the bridge function.

'I will instruct you how it is that they shall beseech their entreaty from the first ones' — transitional promise to teach, not teaching itself. 'The first ones' anticipates the cosmic narrative but this paragraph is frame structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The Great Spirit, the Mother of Life, she claimed and prayed and besought and glorified and praised the first established one, who is the Father. She besought him an entreaty. She claimed of him a request. She received a great gift; she and the many powers with her.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First emanation narrative begins. The Mother of Life petitions the Father — both sides of the mapping are cosmic beings. 'The Great Spirit, the Mother of Life' and 'the first established one, who is the Father' are systematic cosmological nomenclature. The petition-and-granting is cosmic process (emanation through request).

paragraphs.core_text: She besought an entreaty on behalf of the First Man, because of how he had come forth and thrown himself down. He became distant from the Mother of Life. He separated from her and gave himself; in great affliction. He joined war on earth with the destruction and the grief and the weakness; in the worlds of Darkness; in the abysses made of fear; in the midst of the demons' ditch; amongst the powers of the devil!
paragraphs.temporal_note: First Man's descent narrative. All elements within the cosmic system: First Man, Mother of Life, worlds of Darkness, abysses, demons. 'He joined war on earth with the destruction and the grief and the weakness' describes cosmic combat. The five sons' defeat/affliction is core cosmogony.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed, he is like a king standing in the midst of his enemies. And when the Mother of Life petitioned and prayed and glorified and praised the Father, the first established one, she did petition him that he might send a power; a protector and redeemer and helper for the son of God who is set in affliction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the First Man narrative. The simile 'like a king standing in the midst of his enemies' is within the cosmic narrative frame. Mother of Life petitions for a cosmic helper. 'Son of God' here = First Man, a cosmic title within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.273⟩ Now, just as she had besought and interceded, so likewise was her prayer fulfilled and received into the presence of the Father of Greatness. He turned and gave to her her entreaty: the great power, the Living Spirit, the giver of ease. The Mother of Life and the Living Spirit came with great power to the borders of the territory. They brought the First Man up from that war and struggle, wherein he is set.
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Now, just as... so likewise' here narrates the cosmic event resolution — not an editorial bridge to institutional practice. The Father of Greatness emanates the Living Spirit. 'Borders of the territory' is cosmic geography. All actors and locations within the cosmic system. The rescue of the First Man is core cosmogony.

paragraphs.core_text: He gave himself as a grace for the Mother of Life. He became estranged and far from her, the one whom his enemies (place) in great affliction, the one who is in the land of Darkness since he became weak.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues First Man narrative. 'The land of Darkness' is cosmic geography. Describes the First Man's condition before rescue — all within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit grasped and took him in. He freed him. He set him right and gave him ease in the land of rest [...] the Living Spirit, the first giver of ease [...] the will of these three. The welcomer [...] find with the welcomer that [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: The rescue accomplished. 'Land of rest' is cosmic geography. 'The welcomer' is a cosmic figure in the rescue narrative. Heavy lacunae but cosmic content is clear. 'The will of these three' may refer to a triadic cosmic structure.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] a great power [...] of the loved one [...] the First Man who had been far away. He had become distant. She had besought on his behalf. He was set fast in affliction. (The Living Spirit) went to the place of destruction and weakness, the one that freed and redeemed him and gave him ease from the affliction. He set him right with rest and joy. He has himself become rested, with him for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmented but continues the cosmic rescue narrative. 'Place of destruction and weakness' is cosmic geography. All actors (Living Spirit, First Man, Mother of Life implied) are cosmic beings. The rescue and restoration is cosmic process.

'See now, I have taught you the first entreaty that the Mother of Life besought by her prayer.' Meta-commentary on the teaching — editorial summary marking the end of the first archetypal narrative. Parallel structure with ¶23.

Classic editorial bridge: 'This also is the case with the prayer that the faithful saints [...] over the one who has been released from his body. They shall be granted their entreaty just as the Mother of Life was given the entreaty.' Maps cosmic archetype (Mother of Life) → institutional practice (saints praying for the dead). One side reaches outside the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] and they built the universe and completed it with its firmaments, with its wheels, with the ships of light that are in the heights, with its fastenings, with its earths and its walls, with its vessels. They completed the universe and set it right by the fathers of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological description of the universe's construction. 'Firmaments, wheels, ships of light, fastenings, earths, walls, vessels' — cosmic architecture nomenclature. 'Fathers of light' are cosmic beings. Both sides of all descriptions stay within the cosmic system. This bridges between the first and second archetypal narratives.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.274⟩ Then, the Great Spirit stood with the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder with the Living Spirit and the First Man. These five stood to prayer; they glorified and praised the Father, the first established one. They besought of him an entreaty. They claimed of him a request, that he might give them the power [...] the leader, a guide to all the things of activity that they had constructed. That he might come and purify the living soul that is set in affliction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second emanation narrative. The five great cosmic beings (Great Spirit/Mother of Life, Beloved of the Lights, Great Builder, Living Spirit, First Man) petition the Father. This is systematic emanation hierarchy — all five named, their collective petition described. 'The living soul that is set in affliction' is the cosmic condition requiring the Third Ambassador.

paragraphs.core_text: They prayed and besought their Father, and he received from them their prayer [...] he gave them their entreaty and their request [...] he summoned from him [...] which is the Third Ambassador. He, he came from the power of his greatness. He saw the entire soul, how it is entangled in a chain and set fast. It sees the things of activity that his brothers have constructed, that have come from the heights. Again, he saw the living soul, that it is entangled and set fast in a great torture. It is oppressed in the stink of the abyss that is joined with it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The Third Ambassador's emanation and cosmic perception. 'The stink of the abyss' — sensory quality mapped to cosmic geography. 'Entangled in a chain and set fast' — describes the living soul's cosmic condition. 'His brothers' = the five fathers. All within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: And therefore, he, the Ambassador [...] in his charity. So, he revealed his way, before this underworld that is dug deep down, to free the living soul. He redeemed it from all the fleshes of death wherein it is pained. He gave it ease. He set it right in the place of rest and joy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The Ambassador's salvific activity. 'The underworld that is dug deep down,' 'the fleshes of death,' 'place of rest and joy' — cosmic geography and cosmic condition. All within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: And again, he too, the Ambassador, he fulfilled the will of these three; the will of his brothers who had besought the Father for him. They claimed of him a request, together with the [...] of the Father, the one that [...] he gave the entreaty that they had besought of him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the Ambassador fulfilling the cosmic mission requested by his brothers. 'The will of these three' refers to cosmic beings within the hierarchy. Substrate score 0.0 reflects vocabulary pipeline limitations — the content is entirely cosmic process.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the transferral of the living soul that he had freed. He released it and gave it ease from the affliction. He became king and first to the entire body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumeration marker ('The third is...') preserved. Describes the third aspect of the Ambassador's cosmic work: transferral of the living soul. 'He became king and first to the entire body' — cosmic sovereignty. All within the system.

Editorial seam detected. 'Behold, I have instructed you as to the second entreaty' — editorial summary parallel to ¶15. Marks the end of the second archetypal narrative. Meta-commentary, not teaching.

'Now, happen you know this lesson' is editorial formula. Content maps cosmos → institutional practice: 'Each perfect elect and every catechumen who believes... if he beseeches... shall be granted... Just as the entreaty of his fathers was granted.' Institutional language (elect, catechumen, body, faith) with cosmic reference used as justification.

paragraphs.core_text: the third entreaty when they besought him the third time [...] displayed his image [...] he hid his image from the [...] he stood firm [...] they revealed [...] the light [...] the First Man [...] mock [...] to him in [...] which is exalted [...] garment [...] they were freed [...] to him [...] their voice [...] the body [...] prayer [...] it [...] beseech [...] the body [...] beseech [...] she besought [...] in [...] be free [...] Ambassador [...] and also [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Again, let us come to' — editorial transition formula introducing the third archetypal narrative.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third archetypal supplication, extremely fragmented. Opening 'Again, let us come to' is editorial transition. The cosmic content references First Man, Ambassador, image, light, garment — cosmic beings and attributes. Too fragmented to determine much, but the surviving fragments are cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.276⟩ [...] with the living ones and [...] for ever [...] the first [...] from the [...] he gave him the hope [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extremely fragmented. What survives ('the living ones,' 'the first') is cosmic language. Continuation of the third archetypal narrative. Too damaged for confident classification but nothing institutional is visible.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, Jesus the Splendour perfected the will [...] the will [...] they found the light [...] the will of the [...] that he had [...] he gave them the power that is Jesus the Splendour. He granted the will of the elements. [...] for ever. This first [...] he was humbled, he was made free [...] the [...]-ness is displayed to his enemies. He received the hope [...] reveal [...] Jesus the Splendour, the light power [...] and the entreaty of the [...] of light [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Jesus the Splendour as a cosmic being (distinct from historical Jesus). 'The will of the elements,' 'light power' — cosmic vocabulary. This appears to be a fourth archetypal episode or continuation of the third. Fragmented but the surviving content is entirely within the cosmic system.

Editorial seam detected. 'Now, just as this entreaty [...] this is also how [...] Happen you know this' — bridges cosmic archetype to institutional application. 'You are set firm' addresses the audience. Despite heavy fragmentation, the editorial bridge pattern is clear.
Fragmented but 'the petition of the holy church' is clearly institutional vocabulary. The paragraph functions as institutional application.

'Happen you know' is editorial formula. 'Enacted the alms and the remembrance for the person who had come out from the body' — institutional practice (alms, remembrance for the dead). 'His four great victories' introduces an institutional enumeration.

'The first' in the four victories enumeration. Uses substrate vocabulary ('the living soul that is entangled and bound in the entire universe') but deployed to describe the RESULT of institutional practice (alms for the dead). One side of the mapping reaches into institutional practice. The editor borrows cosmic language to legitimate church practice.

Editorial extension flagged. 'The second' in the four victories. 'He shall make rest for the holy church, by the alms that he enacts' — pure institutional: church, alms, children of the church. Substrate vocabulary absent.
Only 8 words survive: 'The third victory is [...] the Father [...]' — continuation of the institutional enumeration. Too fragmented for further analysis.

Fourth victory. Dense institutional vocabulary: 'alms on his behalf and a remembrance for his brother; whether his father or his mother or his son or else his daughter or his relative.' Family relations, alms, remembrance, church — entirely institutional.
High institutional density (19.35). 'The catechumen [...] this alms for a person if he has come out from his body' — institutional practice.
Heavily fragmented. Surviving words include 'catechumen,' 'sin,' 'affliction' — institutional context. Too damaged for detailed analysis.

Heavily fragmented. Mixes some cosmic vocabulary ('living person who is entangled,' 'the light,' 'Cross') with institutional ('catechumen,' 'reward,' 'remembrance'). The cosmic vocabulary serves the institutional argument about the efficacy of prayer for the dead. 'Grant the entreaty and the request of this catechumen' — institutional application.
Worldly analogy for intercession: a person bound for sin, a relative interceding before a master. No cosmic vocabulary at all. Pure editorial composition to illustrate institutional practice.
Only 6 words survive. Continuation of the analogy.

'(Mani) says: You have asked me about...' — dialogue frame summarizing the analogy's premise. Content describes institutional context (sin, intercession, kinsman) but functions as a frame-summary, not teaching.

Resolution of the worldly analogy: the relative intercedes, fills the masters with charity, frees his kinsman. No cosmic vocabulary. Pure institutional composition explaining how intercession works through analogy.

Editorial extension flagged. Applies the analogy to church practice: 'a male and or female catechumen, or a household member... performs a remembrance in the church... the saints beseech for him a sin-entreaty... in the holy church.' Dense institutional vocabulary (22.73). This is the explicit mapping of the analogy onto institutional practice.

Uses substrate cosmological concepts ('living soul,' 'redeemed and purified and attains its first essence,' 'powers of light') but deployed to describe the RESULT of institutional practice (prayer for the dead). 'Forgiveness of sins from the powers of light' — the cosmic beings serve as addressees of institutional petitions. The substrate language has been repurposed by the editor.

Uses substrate cosmic geography ('land of light,' 'land of life and rest') to describe what happens to the soul through institutional intercession. 'Just as ease has come about... this is how' — editorial bridge syntax mapping cosmic → practice. The cosmic vocabulary entered this passage through the editor's composition.

Opens with dialogue frame ('Then speaks the apostle to that catechumen'). Content is Mani's commission to the catechumens: 'make alms-offerings and remembrances,' 'the cup of water,' 'the saints.' Dense institutional vocabulary (17.54). 'Thousands of afflictions and ten thousands of transmigrations' uses cosmic language but in institutional exhortation.
Closing frame: the catechumen praises and gives thanks. 'I am grateful to you my master, with great confessions' — standard closing formula. Mirrors the opening frame.
